rci1_using_msad.detail: Two separate normative models built. Study 1: single site (UCSF), single scanner (Siemens 3T TIM TRIO). Study 2: multi-site; 3 scanning sites (Indiana University, Brigham and Women's Hospital, McLean Hospital) as part of HCP-EP, all using Siemens Prisma 3T.
rci1_using_msad.supporting_text: "HC, non-affective psychosis (NAff-P), and affective psychosis (Aff-P) individuals were scanned at one of three sites (Indiana University [n=80], Brigham and Women's Hospital [n=46], and McLean Hospital [n=43]) as part of the Human Connectome Project-Early Psychosis (HCPEP) study."

rci2_using_epd.detail: Study 2 uses HCP-EP (Human Connectome Project for Early Psychosis) data, publicly available on NIMH Data Archive. Study 1 uses in-house data from UCSF (publicly shared at OSF but not an EPD per the 5-paper threshold).
rci2_using_epd.supporting_text: "Study 2 included HCs, participants with nonaffective psychosis (NAff-P), and participants with affective psychosis (Aff-P) who underwent MRI scanning as part of the HCP-EP (Human Connectome Project for Early Psychosis)." "Data for study 2 (HCP-EP) are publicly available on the NIMH Data Archive [https://nda.nih.gov/], doi: 10.15154/kgg6-yf92/."
rci2_using_epd.location: Hua2025.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Study 2 Participants; ACKNOWLEDGMENTS AND DISCLOSURES

rci3_epd_name.detail: HCP-EP (Human Connectome Project for Early Psychosis) used for Study 2 reference cohort; HCP-EP is a sub-project of the HCP family
rci3_epd_name.supporting_text: "Study 2 included HCs, participants with nonaffective psychosis (NAff-P), and participants with affective psychosis (Aff-P) who underwent MRI scanning as part of the HCP-EP (Human Connectome Project for Early Psychosis)."
rci3_epd_name.location: Hua2025.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Study 2 Participants

rci5_n.detail: Training phase HC for each study; entire HC sample used for regression model fitting. Study 1 HC n=90 at UCSF; Study 2 HC n=56 from HCP-EP across 3 sites.
rci5_n.supporting_text: "HCs (n = 90) did not meet DSM-IV Axis I criteria and did not have a first-degree relative with psychosis." "HCs (n = 56) did not meet DSM-5 criteria for a mood or psychotic disorder"
